idea: Veteran South London driver in his late forties: Estuary working-class, hoarse and gravelly from twenty years of nights. The furthest class from a minister in RP, and the most recognisable sound of British TV hospital drama.
script: Two minutes out! Get the fuck out of the way!
tone: A working-class man in his late forties from South London with a broad, unmistakably English Estuary accent, dropped t's and a rough, hoarse voice worn down by years of night shifts. He is an NHS ambulance driver bellowing through the windscreen at stopped traffic, gripping the wheel. The first line is fast and clipped, a call back to the crew. The second is a full-chested, furious roar, real and desperate, like a gritty British television hospital drama. Close microphone, dry room, voice only.
